chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Rifa'ah, who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The handshake of the believer is superior to the handshake of the angels.'

key_terms.مُصَافَحَة: Handshake or greeting by clasping hands

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of shaking hands with a believer in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith underscores the tangible spiritual weight of physical connection (musafaha) within the Shia tradition, elevating the believer's greeting above that of angels to highlight the sanctity of human community. Scholars often interpret this as a reflection of the believer's unique status as God's vicegerent on earth, making their social bonds a direct conduit for divine grace. This emphasis reinforces the ethical imperative of maintaining strong, affectionate ties (silat al-rahib) among the faithful.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Rifa’at who said,
‘I heard himasws saying: ‘The shaking of the hands of the Momin is superior than the shaking of the hands of the Angels’.
en.sarwar: 21. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Rifa’a who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘A handshake of believing people is better than a handshake of angels.’”
